translations.text: In many portions and in many ways, God spoke long ago to our ancestors through the prophets.
And in these last days he has spoken to us through his Son, whom he appointed heir of everything, and through whom he made the worlds.

He is the radiance of his glory and the image of his being, and he sustains everything by the power of his word. He himself accomplished the cleansing of our sins and sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high.
He has become so much greater than the angels, just as the name he has inherited is more excellent than theirs.
For to which of the angels did God ever say, “You are my Son; today I have fathered you”? And again, “I will be his Father, and he will be my Son.”
And again, when he brings the firstborn into the world, he says, “Let all the angels of God worship him.”
But about the angels he says this: “He made his angels wind, and his servants burning fire.”
But about the Son he says, “Your throne, O God, is yours forever and ever. The scepter of your kingdom is an upright scepter.
You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness. Therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of joy more than your companions.”
And again, “You laid the foundations of the earth in the beginning, and the heavens are the work of your hands.
They will pass away, but you remain, and they will all wear out like clothing.
You will fold them up like a cloak, and they will be changed. But you remain as you are, and your years will never end.”
But to which of the angels did he ever say, “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool beneath your feet”?
Are they not all spirits who serve, sent out to serve those who are to inherit life?
Therefore we must pay much closer attention to what we have heard, so that we do not fall.
For if the message spoken through angels proved firm, and everyone who heard it and violated it received a just punishment,
how will we escape if we disregard the things that are our life? These things were first spoken by our Lord and were confirmed to us by those who heard him,
while God testified to them through signs, wonders, various mighty deeds, and distributions of the Holy Spirit given according to his will.
For it was not to angels that he subjected the world to come, about which we are speaking.
Rather, as Scripture testifies and says, “What is man that you remember him, or the son of man that you care for him?
You made him a little lower than the angels. You placed glory and honor on his head and gave him authority over the work of your hands.
You subjected everything beneath his feet.” Now in subjecting everything to him, he left nothing that was not subjected. But at present we do not yet see everything subjected to him.

But we see the one who was made a little lower than the angels, namely Jesus, because of the suffering of his death, with glory and honor placed on his head. For he, God, in his grace tasted death for everyone.
For it was fitting for the one through whom everything exists and for whose sake everything exists, who brought many sons into glory, to perfect the leader of their life through his suffering.
For the one who made holy and those who were made holy are all from one. Therefore he is not ashamed to call them his brothers,
saying, “I will proclaim your name to my brothers, and in the midst of the assembly I will praise you.”
And again, “I will put my trust in him.” And again, “Here I am, and the children God has given me.”
For since the children shared in flesh and blood, he likewise shared in these same things, so that through his death he might render powerless the one who holds the power of death, that is, Satan,
And free those who, through fear of death, were held in slavery all their lives.
for death did not have authority over angels, but over Abraham’s descendants.
For this reason he had to become like his brothers in every respect, so that he might be merciful and a faithful high priest in matters concerning God, and make atonement for the sins of the people.
For because he himself suffered and was tempted, he can help those who are tempted.
Therefore, my holy brothers, who have been called with a calling from heaven, consider Jesus Christ, the apostle and high priest of our confession.
He is faithful to the one who appointed him, as Moses was in his whole house.
For this one’s glory is far greater than that of Moses, just as the honor of the builder of a house is far greater than that of the building.
For every house is built by someone, but the one who builds everything is God.
Moses was entrusted with the whole house as a servant, as a testimony to the things that were to be spoken through him.
But Christ is over his house as a son. And we are his house, if we hold on to our confidence and our proud hope in him until the end.
For the Holy Spirit said, “Today, if you hear his voice,”
Do not harden your hearts and provoke him, as those who rebelled did, and as on the day of testing in the wilderness,
where your ancestors tested me and put me to the proof, and saw my deeds for forty years.
“For this reason I was disgusted with that generation and said, ‘They are a people whose hearts go astray, and they have not known my ways.’
And as I swore in my anger, ‘They will not enter my rest.’”
So be watchful, my brothers, lest any of you have an evil, unbelieving heart, and you turn away from the living God.
Instead, encourage one another every day, as long as it is called “today,” so that none of you may be hardened by the deception of sin.
For we have been joined with Christ, if we persevere in this firm covenant from beginning to end.
As it is said, “Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts and provoke him.”
For who were those who heard and angered him? Were they not all those who came out of Egypt through Moses?
And with whom was he disgusted for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose bones fell in the wilderness?
And concerning whom did he swear that they would not enter his rest, if not those who refused to obey?
And we see that they could not enter because they did not believe.
Let us therefore be afraid that, while the promise of entering his rest still stands, any of you may be found to have failed to enter.
For we too received the good news, just as they did. But the message they heard did not benefit them, because it was not mixed with faith in those who heard it.
But we who have believed enter the rest, just as he said, “As I swore in my anger, ‘They will not enter my rest.’” Yet God’s works had been done from the beginning of the world.
As he said concerning the Sabbath, “God rested on the seventh day from all his works.”
And here again he said, “They will not enter my rest.”
Since, then, there was room for some to enter it, and those who first received the good news did not enter because they did not obey,
Again, after a long time, he appoints another day, as it is written above that David said: “Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts.”
For if Joshua son of Nun had given them rest, he would not have spoken afterward about another day.
So a Sabbath rest remains for the people of God.
For whoever has entered his rest has also rested from his own works, just as God rested from his.
Let us therefore make every effort to enter that rest, so that we do not fall as those who disobeyed did.

For the word of God is alive and accomplishes everything. It is much sharper than a double-edged sword, penetrating to the division of soul and spirit, of joints, marrow, and bones. It judges the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
No creature is hidden from him, but everything is naked and exposed before the eyes of the one to whom we must give an account.
Therefore, since we have a great high priest, Jesus Christ, the Son of God, who ascended to heaven, let us hold firmly to our confession of him.
For we do not have a high priest who cannot sympathize with our weakness, but one who has been tested in everything as we are, yet without sin.
Let us therefore approach the throne of his grace with confidence, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help us in a time of distress.
For every high priest who comes from among human beings acts on their behalf in matters concerning God, to offer gifts and sacrifices for sins.
He can humble himself and sympathize with those who do not know and go astray, because he too is clothed in weakness.
Because of this, he is obligated to make offerings for his own sins, just as he does for the people.
No one takes this honor for himself, but only someone called by God, as Aaron was.
Likewise, Christ did not glorify himself to become high priest. Rather, it was the one who said to him, “You are my Son; today I have fathered you.”
As he also said in another place, “You are a priest forever in the likeness of Melchizedek.”
While he was clothed in flesh, he offered prayers and pleas with loud cries and tears to the one who could save him from death, and he was heard.
Although he was the Son, he learned obedience from the fear and sufferings he endured.
And so he was made perfect and became the source of eternal life for all who obey him,
and he was named by God a high priest in the likeness of Melchizedek.
Now concerning this Melchizedek, we have much to say, and it is difficult to explain, because you have become dull in your hearing.

For you ought to have become teachers, since you have spent so much time learning. But now you again need to learn the elementary writings that form the beginning of God's message. You have come to need milk rather than solid food.
Everyone whose food is milk is unfamiliar with the teaching about righteousness, because he is a child.
But solid food is for the mature, whose senses have been trained through practice to distinguish good from evil.
Therefore, let us leave the elementary teaching about Christ and move on to maturity. Or will you lay another foundation again for repentance from dead works and faith in God,
and for teaching about baptism and the laying on of hands, the resurrection from the dead, and eternal judgment?
If the Lord permits, we will do this.
But those who once went down into baptism, tasted the gift from heaven, and received the Holy Spirit,
and tasted the good word of God and the power of the age to come,
cannot, if they sin again, be renewed once more to repentance and crucify the Son of God again and disgrace him.
For land that drinks the rain that often falls on it and produces plants useful to those for whose sake it is cultivated receives a blessing from God.
But if it produces thorns and thistles, it is rejected and is not far from a curse; its end is burning.
But we are confident of better things concerning you, my brothers, things that are close to salvation, even though we speak this way.
For God is not unjust, so as to forget your deeds and the love you have shown in his name by serving the saints and continuing to serve them.
But we want each one of you to show this same diligence, so that your hope may be fulfilled to the very end,
and that you may not lose heart, but imitate those who through faith and patience became heirs of the promise.
For when God made a promise to Abraham, since he had no one greater than himself by whom to swear, he swore by himself,
and said, “I will certainly bless you and greatly multiply you.”
And so he waited patiently and received the promise.
For people swear by someone greater than themselves, and every dispute that arises among them is brought to a firm conclusion by oaths.
For this reason, God wished all the more to show the heirs of the promise that his pledge does not change, and he bound it with oaths.
So that through two things that do not change, in which God cannot lie, we who have taken refuge in him may have great encouragement and hold on to the hope promised to us.
It is like an anchor for us, holding our soul so that it will not be shaken, and entering inside beyond the curtain,
where Jesus entered ahead of us on our behalf and became a priest forever in the likeness of Melchizedek.
Now this Melchizedek is king of Salem, priest of God Most High. He met Abraham as he returned from the battle against the kings and blessed him.
Abraham set aside for him a tenth of everything he had with him. His name means “king of righteousness,” and he is also king of Salem, which means “king of peace.”
Neither his father nor his mother was recorded in the genealogies, nor the beginning of his days nor the end of his life. Rather, in the likeness of the Son of God, his priesthood continues forever.
Consider how great this man is: Abraham, the patriarch, gave him a tenth of the choicest things.
For those descendants of Levi who received the priesthood had a command in the law to collect tithes from the people—that is, from their own brothers—even though they too were descended from Abraham.
But this man, who is not recorded in their genealogies, collected tithes from Abraham and blessed the one who had received the promise.
Now it is beyond dispute that the lesser is blessed by the greater.
Here, people who die collect tithes, but there, the one who collects them is someone whom Scripture testifies is alive.
And, one might say, through Abraham even Levi, who collected tithes, himself paid tithes.
For he was still in his father's loins when his father met Melchizedek.

So if perfection had been possible through the Levitical priesthood, under which the law was established for the people, why was another priest needed to arise in the likeness of Melchizedek? Yet he said that he would be in the likeness of Aaron.
But just as there was a change in the priesthood, so there was also a change in the law.
For the one about whom these things were said was born into another tribe, from which no one had ever served at the altar.
For it is clear that our Lord arose from Judah, a tribe about which Moses said nothing concerning the priesthood.
And this is even more clearly known from what he said: another priest arises in the likeness of Melchizedek,
one who becomes a priest not by a law of bodily commandments, but by the power of a life that cannot be ended.
For he testifies about him, “You are a priest forever in the likeness of Melchizedek.”
The former commandment was changed because of its weakness and because there was no benefit in it.
For the law made nothing perfect. But in its place a better hope came in, through which we draw near to God.
And he confirmed it for us with oaths.

For those men became priests without oaths, but this one with oaths, as he said to him through David: “The Lord has sworn and will not go back on his word: You are a priest forever in the likeness of Melchizedek.”
By this much, the covenant for which Jesus became the guarantor is better.
Those priests were many because they died and were not allowed to continue.
But because this one remains forever, his priesthood does not pass away,
and he is able to save forever those who draw near to God through him. For he is always alive and offers prayer on their behalf.
For such a priest was indeed fitting for us: pure, without evil, without defilement, separate from sins, and exalted above the heavens.
He has no need, like the high priests, to offer sacrifices every day, first for his own sins and then for the people. For he did this once when he offered himself.
For the law appoints weak human beings as priests, but the word of the oaths, which came after the law, appoints the Son, who is perfect forever.
Now the main point of all this is that we have a high priest who sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in heaven.
And he became a minister of the sanctuary and of the true tabernacle, which God set up, not a human being.
For every high priest is appointed to offer gifts and sacrifices. Therefore it was necessary for this one also to have something to offer.
If he were on earth, he would not even be a priest, because there were priests who offered gifts according to the law.

They serve a likeness and shadows of the things in heaven, just as Moses was told when he was making the tabernacle: “See that you make everything according to the pattern shown to you on the mountain.”

But now Jesus Christ has received a ministry superior to that one, just as the covenant of which he has been made mediator is also superior and was given with better promises than those of the former covenant.
For if the first covenant had been without fault, there would have been no place for this second one.
For he finds fault with them and says, “Look, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will establish a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah,

not like the covenant I gave their ancestors on the day I took them by the hand and brought them out of the land of Egypt. Because they did not remain in my covenant, I too disregarded them, says the Lord.

But this is the covenant I will give the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: I will put my law in their minds and write it on their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be my people.
No one will teach his fellow citizen or his brother, saying, ‘Know the Lord,’ because they will all know me, from their youngest to their oldest.
I will forgive their wrongdoing and will no longer remember their sins.”
By saying “new,” he has made the first covenant old. And what has become old and aged is close to passing away.
Now the first covenant had regulations for worship and an earthly sanctuary.
For the first part of the tabernacle that was constructed contained the lampstand, the table, and the bread of the Presence. It was called the Holy Place.
The inner part of the tabernacle, beyond the second entrance, was called the Holy of Holies.

It contained a golden incense burner and the ark of the covenant, covered entirely with gold. In the ark were a golden jar containing manna, Aaron’s staff that had sprouted, and the tablets of the covenant.
Above it were the cherubim of glory, overshadowing the atonement cover. But this is not the time to speak individually about each of these things that were arranged in this way.
The priests regularly entered the outer part of the tabernacle and performed their service.
But into its inner part only the high priest entered, once a year, with the blood that he offered for himself and for the sins the people committed in ignorance.
By this the Holy Spirit was making known that the way into the sanctuary had not yet been revealed as long as the first tabernacle remained standing.
This was a symbol for that time, when offerings and sacrifices were presented that could not perfect the conscience of the person offering them,
but concerned only food and drink and various kinds of washings. These are regulations for the body, imposed until the time of reform.

But Christ came and became the high priest of the good things he accomplished. He entered the greater and more perfect tabernacle, which was not made by human hands and did not belong to this creation.
He did not enter with the blood of goats and calves, but with his own blood he entered the sanctuary once and obtained eternal redemption.
For if the blood of goats and calves and the ashes of a heifer were sprinkled on those who were defiled, and sanctified them so that their bodies were clean,
how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without blemish to God, cleanse our conscience from dead works so that we may serve the living God!

For this reason he became the mediator of a new covenant. Through his death he brought redemption to those who transgressed the first covenant, so that those called to an eternal inheritance might receive the promise.
For where there is a will, it makes known the death of the person who made it.
It becomes valid only upon death, because as long as the person who made it is alive, it has no effect.
For this reason, not even the first covenant was established without blood.
For when Moses had given all the commandments in the law to all the people, Moses took the blood of a heifer and water, with scarlet wool and hyssop, and sprinkled the books and all the people.
He said to them, “This is the blood of the covenant that God commanded for you.”
He also sprinkled some of the blood on the tabernacle and all the utensils used in its service.
For everything is cleansed with blood under the law, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.
It is therefore necessary that these things, which are copies of heavenly things, be cleansed by these means, but the heavenly things themselves by sacrifices better than these.
For Christ did not enter a sanctuary made by human hands, which is a copy of the true one. Instead, he entered heaven itself to appear before God on our behalf,
not to offer himself many times, as the high priest used to do, entering the sanctuary every year with blood that was not his own.
Otherwise, he would have had to suffer many times since the beginning of the world. But now, at the end of the world, he has offered himself once in sacrifice to abolish sin.
And just as human beings are appointed to die once, and after their death comes judgment,
so Christ too was offered once, and in his own person he sacrificed the sins of many. He will appear a second time, without sins, to bring salvation to those who wait for him.

For the law contained a shadow of the good things to come, not the actual reality of those things. Therefore, the same sacrifices offered year after year could never make those who offered them perfect.
For if they had made them perfect, they would surely have stopped offering them, because those who had been cleansed once would no longer have been troubled by their conscience about sins.
Instead, through those sacrifices they are reminded of their sins every year.
For the blood of bulls and goats cannot cleanse sins.
Therefore, when he entered the world, he said, “You did not desire sacrifices and offerings, but you clothed me with a body.
You did not ask for whole burnt offerings for sins.
Then I said, ‘Here I am; I am coming—as it is written about me at the beginning of the book—to do your will, O God.’”
Above he said, “You did not desire sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings for sins”—the things that were offered according to the law.
And afterward he said, “Here I am coming to do your will, O God.” By this he abolished the first to establish the second.
For by this will of his we have been made holy through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
For every high priest who stood ministering daily offered the same sacrifices again and again, sacrifices that could never cleanse sins.
But this one offered a single sacrifice for sins and sat down at the right hand of God forever.
From then on he waits until his enemies are made a footstool beneath his feet.
For by one offering he has made perfect forever those who are made holy through him.
The Holy Spirit also testifies to us, saying:
“This is the covenant that I will give them after those days, says the Lord: I will put my law in their minds and write it on their hearts.
And I will not remember their wrongdoing and their sins against them.”
Now where there is forgiveness of sins, an offering for sins is no longer required.
Therefore, my brothers, we have confidence to enter the sanctuary through the blood of Jesus,
and a way of life that he has now opened anew for us through the curtain, which is his flesh.
And we have a great priest over the house of God.
Therefore, let us draw near with a sincere heart and the confidence of faith, with our hearts sprinkled and cleansed from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.
Let us hold firmly to the confession of our hope without wavering, for the one who promised us is faithful.
And let us pay attention to one another, encouraging love and good deeds.
Let us not abandon our gathering together, as some are in the habit of doing, but encourage one another, all the more as you see that day drawing near.
For if someone sins deliberately after receiving the knowledge of the truth, there is no longer a sacrifice to be offered for sins.
Instead, a terrifying judgment awaits, and a fury of fire that consumes the enemies.
For if someone who violates the law of Moses dies without mercy on the testimony of two or three witnesses,

how much greater a punishment do you think someone will receive who has trampled on the Son of God, regarded the blood of his covenant, by which he was made holy, as anyone else's blood, and insulted the Spirit of grace?
We know the one who said, “Vengeance is mine, and I will repay,” and again, “The Lord will judge his people.”
It is a very fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
So remember the earlier days, when you received baptism and endured a great struggle of suffering through insults and afflictions,
and when you were made public spectacles. You also stood alongside people who endured these things.

You felt compassion for those who were imprisoned, and you joyfully endured the plundering of your possessions, because you know that you have a possession in heaven that is better and does not pass away.
So do not throw away your confidence, for a great reward awaits it.
For you need endurance, so that you may do God's will and receive what was promised.
For in a little while, a very short time, the one who is coming will come and will not delay.
But the righteous person will live by faith in me, and if he loses heart, my soul takes no pleasure in him.
But we do not belong to the discouragement that leads to destruction, but to the faith that preserves our lives.
Now faith is confidence concerning the things hoped for, as though they had already happened, and a revelation of things that are not seen.
Through this, testimony was given in favor of the people of old.
For by faith we understand that the worlds were established by the word of God, and that the things that are seen came from things that are not seen.

By faith Abel offered God a sacrifice far better than Cain's. Because of it, testimony was given that he was righteous, and God testified about his offering. Through it he speaks even though he is dead.
By faith Enoch was taken away and did not taste death. He could not be found, because God had taken him away. For before he was taken away, testimony was given that he had pleased God.
But without faith no one can please God. For whoever approaches God must believe that he exists and that he rewards those who seek him.

By faith Noah, when he was told about things that were not yet seen, acted in fear and built an ark to save the lives of his household. Through it he condemned the world and became an heir of the righteousness that comes through faith.
By faith Abraham, when he was called, obeyed and went out to the place he was to receive as an inheritance. He went out without knowing where he was going.
By faith he lived as a foreign resident in the land promised to him, as though it were a foreign land. He lived in tents with Isaac and Jacob, who were fellow heirs with him of the promise.
For he was waiting for the city that has foundations, whose designer and builder is God.
By faith Sarah too, who was barren, received the strength to conceive, and she gave birth beyond her childbearing years, because she considered the one who had promised her to be faithful.
Therefore, from one man whose strength had failed through old age, descendants were born as numerous as the stars in heaven and as the sand on the seashore, which cannot be counted.

All these died in faith without receiving what was promised to them. But they saw it from a distance and rejoiced in it, and they acknowledged that they were strangers and temporary residents on earth.
Those who say such things show that they are seeking a city of their own.
If they had been seeking the city they had left, they would have had time to return to it.
But now it is clear that they were longing for a better city, the one in heaven. Therefore God is not ashamed to be called their God, for he has prepared a city for them.
By faith Abraham offered Isaac when he was tested, and brought his only son to the altar—the one he had received through a promise.
For he had been told, “Through Isaac your descendants will be named.”
He reasoned within himself that God had the power even to raise the dead. Therefore, figuratively speaking, Isaac was given back to him.
By faith in what was to come, Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau.
By faith Jacob, as he was dying, blessed each of Joseph’s sons and worshiped, leaning on the top of his staff.
By faith Joseph, as he was dying, spoke of the departure of the people of Israel and gave instructions about his bones.
By faith Moses’ parents hid him for three months after he was born, because they saw that the child was beautiful, and they were not afraid of the king’s command.
By faith Moses, when he became a man, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter.
He chose to suffer with God’s people rather than enjoy sin for a short time.
He considered the disgrace of Christ to be far greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt, for he was looking ahead to the reward.
By faith he left Egypt and was not afraid of the king’s anger. He endured as though he could see God, who cannot be seen.
By faith he observed the Passover and the sprinkling of blood, so that the one who was destroying the firstborn would not come near them.
By faith they crossed the Red Sea as though on dry land. But the Egyptians were swallowed up in it when they dared to cross it.
By faith the walls of Jericho fell after they had been encircled for seven days.
By faith Rahab the prostitute did not perish with those who disobeyed, because she welcomed the spies in peace.
And what more shall I say? For I have too little time to tell about Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and the rest of the prophets.
Through faith they conquered kingdoms, practiced righteousness, received promises, and shut the mouths of lions.
They quenched the power of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, recovered strength after illnesses, became mighty in battle, and overthrew the camps of their enemies.
They gave women back their sons, raised from the dead. Others died under torture and did not look for deliverance, so that they might have a better resurrection.
Others endured mockery and beatings. Others were handed over to chains and imprisonment.
Others were stoned; others were sawn apart; others died by the edge of the sword. Others wandered about dressed in sheepskins and goatskins, needy, oppressed, and mistreated.
They were people of whom the world was not worthy. They wandered through deserts and mountains, in caves and holes in the earth.
All these, whose faith was attested, did not receive the promise,
because God had made provision beforehand for our benefit, so that they would not be made perfect without us.

Therefore, since we too have all these witnesses surrounding us like a cloud, let us throw off every burden, as well as the sin that is always lying in wait for us, and let us run with endurance the race set before us.
Let us look to Jesus, who became the founder and perfecter of our faith. Instead of the joy he had, he endured the cross, disregarded its shame, and sat down at the right hand of God's throne.
Consider, then, how much he endured from those sinners who were opposing their own souls, so that you do not grow weary or lose heart.
In your struggle against sin, you have not yet reached the point of shedding blood.
And you have forgotten the teaching that addresses you as sons: “My son, do not neglect the Lord's discipline, and do not lose heart when he corrects you.
For the Lord disciplines those he loves, and he lashes the sons in whom he delights.”
Therefore, endure discipline, because God treats you as sons. For what son is there whom his father does not discipline?
But if you are without the discipline that everyone receives, then you are outsiders and not sons.
And if our earthly fathers disciplined us and we respected them, how much more should we submit to the Father of spirits and live?
For they disciplined us for a short time as they wished, but God disciplines us for our benefit, so that we may share in his holiness.
No discipline seems joyful at the time, but painful. Later, however, it produces the fruits of peace and righteousness for those who have been trained by it.
Therefore, strengthen your limp hands and trembling knees.
Make straight paths for your feet, so that the lame limb will not be dislocated but healed.
Pursue peace with everyone, and pursue holiness, without which no one sees our Lord.
Be watchful, lest anyone among you be found lacking God's grace, or lest a bitter root sprout, harm you, and defile many through it,
or lest anyone among you be found sexually immoral or irreligious like Esau, who sold his birthright for a single meal.
For you know that even afterward, when he wanted to inherit the blessing, he was rejected. For he found no opportunity for repentance, though he sought it with tears.
For you have not approached a fire that burns and can be touched, nor darkness, thick gloom, and a storm,
nor the sound of a trumpet and the sound of words whose hearers begged that no more should be spoken to them.
For they could not bear what they were commanded: “Even if an animal approaches the mountain, it must be stoned.”
And the sight was so terrifying that Moses said, “I am afraid and trembling.”
But you have approached Mount Zion and the city of the living God, Jerusalem in heaven, and gatherings of tens of thousands of angels,
and the assembly of the firstborn who are registered in heaven, and God, the judge of all, and the spirits of the righteous who have been made perfect,
and Jesus, the mediator of a new covenant, and the sprinkling of his blood, which speaks better than Abel’s.

Therefore, take care not to refuse the one who speaks to you. For if those who refused the one who spoke to them on earth did not escape, how much less will we escape if we refuse the one who speaks to us from heaven?
His voice shook the earth. But now he has promised, saying, “Once more I will shake not only the earth but also heaven.”
Now his saying “once” indicates the transformation of the things that are shaken, because they are created things, so that the things that are not shaken may remain.
Therefore, since we have received a kingdom that cannot be shaken, let us hold on to grace, through which we may serve and please God with reverence and fear.
For our God is a consuming fire.
Let love for one another as brothers and sisters continue among you.
And do not forget hospitality to strangers, for through it some people were privileged to welcome angels without knowing it.
Remember those who are imprisoned as though you were imprisoned with them. Remember those who are oppressed, since you yourselves are people clothed in flesh.
Marriage is honored in every respect, and their marriage bed is pure. But God judges the sexually immoral and adulterers.
Do not let your mind be set on loving money, but be content with what you have. For the Lord himself has said, “I will not leave you, nor withdraw my hands from you.”
And we can say confidently, “The Lord is my helper; I will not be afraid. What can a human being do to me?”
Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you. Consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith.
Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever.
Do not be led away by strange and varied teachings. For it is good for us to strengthen our hearts by grace, not by foods, because those who followed such practices gained no benefit from them.
But we have an altar from which those who serve in the tabernacle have no right to eat.
For the animals whose blood the high priest used to bring into the sanctuary for sins had their flesh burned outside the camp.
For this reason Jesus also suffered outside the city, to make his people holy through his blood.
Therefore, let us also go out to him outside the camp, bearing his disgrace.
For we have no lasting city here, but we look forward to the one that is to come.
And through him let us continually offer sacrifices of praise to God, that is, the fruit of lips that acknowledge his name.
And do not forget compassion and sharing with the poor, for through such sacrifices a person pleases God.
Obey your leaders and submit to them, for they keep watch over your souls as people who must give an account of you. Let them do this with joy and not with groaning, for that would not benefit you.
Pray for us, for we are confident that we have a good conscience, desiring to conduct ourselves well in everything.
I urge you all the more to do this, so that I may be restored to you soon.
Now may the God of peace, who brought up from the dead the great shepherd of the flock through the blood of the everlasting covenant, Jesus Christ our Lord—
may he make you complete in every good work so that you may do his will. And may he accomplish in us what is pleasing to him through Jesus Christ, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.
Now I ask you, my brothers, to bear patiently with this word of encouragement, for I have written to you briefly.
Know that our brother Timothy has been released. If he comes soon, I will see you with him.
Greet all your leaders and all the saints. All those from Italy greet you.
Grace be with you all. Amen.
